provenance.quote:

In 2008 and 2016, pursuant to Public Act 49 of 2008, Wayne County voters renewed a 10-year property tax millage to fund zoological services through the Wayne County Zoological Authority,
supporting animal care for more than 2,000 animals and 200 species, educational and senior programs, and facility maintenance at the Detroit Zoo.

To continue providing these services, the Authority seeks to renew and restore the millage to the original voter-approved rate of 0.10 mill (10 cents per $1,000 of taxable value). This proposal would
renew the millage at 0.0982 mill and restore the remaining 0.0018 mill that was reduced due to required rollback, for a total authorized rate of 0.10 mill on taxable real and personal property for ten
(10) years.

funds are subject to annual independent audits. It is estimated that $6,145,462 will be collected in the first year.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews 0.0982 mill and restores 0.0018 mill for a total 0.10 mill property tax supporting the Detroit Zoo for 2028–2037. Estimated first-year collections are $6,145,462. Funds go through the Zoological Authority and are subject to annual independent audits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the renewal and restoration to 0.10 mill.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adds a 0.2 mill tax on taxable Wayne County property for 2026–2035 for historical museum services, including the Charles H. Wright, Detroit Historical and Dossin Great Lakes museums. Estimated 2026 collections are $12,219,200; after authority administration costs, 15% of Wayne County revenue returns to the county to support historical museums.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the ten-year historical museum tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adds up to 3.5 mills on taxable real and personal property for 2027–2031 for police, fire and emergency services, personnel, benefits, equipment and capital replacement. Estimated first-year revenue at the full rate is $672,281.68; some revenue may be captured by the Downtown Development Authority.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the five-year additional public safety millage.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes annual special assessments up to 1.25 mills on nonexempt real property to equip, maintain and operate police and fire services. Levies run 2026–2029 to fund 2027–2030. The estimated first-year revenue if fully levied in December 2026 is $613,750.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the four-year special assessment.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adds 0.65 mill for 2027–2033 to maintain, repair, improve and extend the life of parks and recreation facilities. Estimated first-year revenue is $562,000; a portion is disbursed to the Downtown Development and Tax Increment Financing authorities.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the seven-year parks and recreation millage.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Restores the city’s operating-tax limit from about 17.17 mills to up to 20 mills by overriding required Headlee reductions. The official question estimates $2,420,265 in 2027 revenue from this restored authority.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve restoration of the operating-tax limit to 20 mills.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes a public sale of up to 80 acres of the approximately 248.5-acre Highlands Golf Course to the highest qualified bidder, subject to City Council approval, for a community park and about 400 housing units. The portion is west of the Forest Subdivision and north of King Road.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the proposed land sale under the stated conditions.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes up to $10 million in general-obligation unlimited-tax bonds for city road improvements, including water-main replacements, land and rights-of-way. Each series may run no more than ten years. Estimated tax rates are 2.5211 mills in 2027 and a 2.5229 mill simple annual average to repay the bonds.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the road-improvement bonds.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Restores 1.9055 mills for 2026–2035, raising the authorized city operating-tax limit from 15.9814 to 17.8869 mills. Revenue from the restored portion is dedicated exclusively to roads, streets, bridges, sidewalks and transportation infrastructure. Estimated 2026 revenue is $102,761.42.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the restored millage and transportation dedication.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Removes charter term limits for the mayor, city clerk, city treasurer and City Council.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Remove the stated term limits.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Requires sealed competitive bids for purchases, public improvements and contracts costing 0.1% or more of the annual city operating budget. Council must set annual thresholds for its own approval of transactions and may adjust them by resolution when adopting the budget.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt the budget-based bidding rule and annual approval thresholds.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews up to 2 mills annually for 2027–2036 for parks and recreation operations, including youth and senior programs. The official estimate is $580,000 in revenue if the maximum is levied and an average homeowner cost of $54.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Renew the ten-year parks and recreation millage.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews up to 1 mill annually for 2027–2036 for senior services operations. The official estimate is $290,000 in revenue if the maximum is levied and an average homeowner cost of $27.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Renew the ten-year senior services millage.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews the rolled-back 0.1439 mill rate for 2026–2035 to maintain township bike paths. Estimated first-year revenue is $119,000; portions go to the Downtown Development and Brownfield authorities as legally required.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Renew the ten-year bike path millage.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews the rolled-back 0.4818 mill rate for 2026–2030 for fire vehicles and equipment. Estimated first-year revenue is $403,000, including about $5,750 disbursed to the Downtown Development Authority and $1,800 to the Brownfield Authority.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Renew the five-year fire equipment millage.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews the rolled-back 0.4818 mill rate for 2026–2030 to operate the township recreation program. Estimated first-year revenue is $400,000; portions go to the Downtown Development and Brownfield authorities as legally required.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Renew the five-year recreation millage.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adds up to 0.10 mill for 2026–2028 to maintain and repair public greenways, open-space property and trails. Estimated first-year revenue is $83,614; a small portion goes to the Downtown Development and Brownfield authorities as legally required.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the three-year additional greenways millage.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews up to 5 mills for 2026–2029 for police protection and Police Department operations and maintenance. Estimated first-year revenue is $2,428,884.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Renew the four-year police millage.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes up to $1.51 billion in bonds for new and renovated schools, facilities, safety/security, technology, sites and buses under the facilities plan. Each series may last up to 30 years. Estimated millage is 3.14 in the first year and a 5.67 annual average. Audited bond proceeds cannot fund salaries, repairs, maintenance or other operating expenses.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the school-improvement bonds.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes 12 mills of restoration authority for 2026–2030, levied only as needed to restore constitutional rollbacks and maintain the 18 mill statutory operating rate. Principal residences and other legally exempt property are excluded. Estimated 2026 revenue from the proposal is $225,346.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the limited restoration authority.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes up to $30 million in bonds for school buildings, equipment, technology, buses, athletic and play facilities and sites. Each series may last up to 25 years. Estimated 2027 millage is 1.21, with no net increase over the prior year; estimated average repayment millage is 2.72. Proceeds are audited and cannot fund salaries, repairs, maintenance or operating expenses.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the school bonds.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews 2.5 mills of hold-harmless operating authority for 2027–2036 on all property except property exempted by law. The previous authorization expires with the 2026 levy. Estimated 2027 revenue is $745,254.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Renew the ten-year hold-harmless operating millage.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Replaces, restores and extends operating authority for 2026–2035. Although 20 mills are authorized, no more than 18 may be levied, with two mills available for future rollbacks. Principal residences and legally exempt property are excluded. The proposal replaces 17.5603 mills and restores 0.4397 mill; its official 2026 revenue estimate is $420,661.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the replacement and restoration authority within the 18 mill levy cap.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes 1.6547 mills of restoration authority for 2027–2035, levied only as necessary to restore constitutional rollbacks and maintain the 18 mill statutory operating rate. Principal residences and other legally exempt property are excluded. The official question estimates $0 in 2027 collections from this additional authority.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the limited restoration authority.
